**James Edward Ryan** (born September 21, 1966) is an American legal scholar. He served as the 9th president of the [University of Virginia](/wiki/University_of_Virginia "University of Virginia") from August 1, 2018, to July 11, 2025. He served as the 11th dean of the [Harvard Graduate School of Education](/wiki/Harvard_Graduate_School_of_Education "Harvard Graduate School of Education") from 2013 to 2018.

Ryan was raised in [Midland Park, New Jersey](/wiki/Midland_Park,_New_Jersey "Midland Park, New Jersey"), attending local public schools.[[1]](#cite_note-1) He graduated from [Yale University](/wiki/Yale_University "Yale University") and the [University of Virginia School of Law](/wiki/University_of_Virginia_School_of_Law "University of Virginia School of Law"), where he was a member of [Omicron Delta Kappa](/wiki/Omicron_Delta_Kappa "Omicron Delta Kappa").

Ryan Fitzpatrick :: College career :: chunk_0001
While an economics student at [Harvard University](/wiki/Harvard_University "Harvard University"), Fitzpatrick had five starts for the [Crimson](/wiki/Harvard_Crimson_football "Harvard Crimson football") during the 2001 and 2002 seasons, working as the backup for Neil Rose.[[6]](#cite_note-6) In 2002, Fitzpatrick recorded 1,155 passing yards with eight touchdowns and no interceptions to go along with 523 rushing yards and five touchdowns.

After Rose graduated in 2003, Fitzpatrick took over the starting job and finished his junior campaign with 1,770 yards, 16 touchdowns, and eight interceptions in seven games. Additionally, he ran for 430 yards and six touchdowns, leading his team to a 7–3 record.[[7]](#cite_note-7)

In 2004, Fitzpatrick was named the [Ivy League](/wiki/Ivy_League "Ivy League") Player of the Year and winner of the George H. "Bulger" Lowe Award, as he accumulated 1,986 yards with 13 touchdowns and six interceptions. Fitzpatrick also led Harvard to a 10–0 record, thus winning the Ivy League Championship.[[8]](#cite_note-8) He ranked second on the team with 448 rushing yards and five scores.

For his career, Fitzpatrick ranked third on Harvard's career list for pass completions, touchdowns, and passing yards. Fitzpatrick's 1,006 total plays for 6,721 yards in total offense broke the old school career records of 1,005 plays by Mike Giardi (1991–93) and 6,519 yards by Neil Rose. (His total plays record has since been surpassed.)[[9]](#cite_note-9) Fitzpatrick was also the school's first quarterback to rush for over 1,000 career yards.[[10]](#cite_note-10)

fanoutqa_016376.x:
The Amazing Spider-Man 2 :: part 02 :: chunk_0001
Development of *The Amazing Spider-Man 2* began after the success of *[The Amazing Spider-Man](/wiki/The_Amazing_Spider-Man_(film) "The Amazing Spider-Man (film)")*. DeHaan, Giamatti, [Felicity Jones](/wiki/Felicity_Jones "Felicity Jones"), and [Chris Cooper](/wiki/Chris_Cooper "Chris Cooper") were cast between December 2012 and February 2013. Filming took place in New York City from February to June 2013. The film was released in 2D, [3D](/wiki/3D_film "3D film"), [RealD 3D](/wiki/RealD_3D "RealD 3D"), and [IMAX 3D](/wiki/IMAX_3D "IMAX 3D") on May 2, 2014 in the United States by [Sony Pictures Releasing](/wiki/Sony_Pictures_Releasing "Sony Pictures Releasing") through its [Columbia Pictures](/wiki/Columbia_Pictures "Columbia Pictures") label, with two international premieres being held between March 31 and April 10 of that year. The film grossed $716.9 million worldwide, making it the [ninth-highest-grossing film of 2014](/wiki/2014_in_film#Highest-grossing_films "2014 in film").

The *Amazing Spider-Man* film series was originally intended to continue with at least two more sequels, as well as several spin-off films featuring other characters. In February 2015, Sony Pictures and [Marvel Studios](/wiki/Marvel_Studios "Marvel Studios") initiated a deal to share the [*Spider-Man* film rights](/wiki/Spider-Man_in_film "Spider-Man in film") and reboot the character within the [Marvel Cinematic Universe](/wiki/Marvel_Cinematic_Universe "Marvel Cinematic Universe") (MCU), cancelling future projects in the *Amazing Spider-Man* series. [Tom Holland](/wiki/Tom_Holland "Tom Holland") succeeded Garfield as [Peter Parker / Spider-Man](/wiki/Peter_Parker_(Marvel_Cinematic_Universe) "Peter Parker (Marvel Cinematic Universe)") in *[Captain America: Civil War](/wiki/Captain_America:_Civil_War "Captain America: Civil War")* (2016) before leading a new series of [*Spider-Man* films set in the MCU](/wiki/Spider-Man_in_film#Licensing_agreement_with_Marvel_Studios "Spider-Man in film"), beginning with *[Spider-Man: Homecoming](/wiki/Spider-Man:_Homecoming "Spider-Man: Homecoming")* (2017). Both Garfield and Foxx reprised their roles

At the [78th Academy Awards](/wiki/78th_Academy_Awards "78th Academy Awards"), *Crash* won the Oscar for [Best Picture](/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Picture "Academy Award for Best Picture"), triumphing over the heavily favored *[Brokeback Mountain](/wiki/Brokeback_Mountain "Brokeback Mountain")* in what is considered as one of the most notable Oscars upsets.[[57]](#cite_note-57)[[58]](#cite_note-58) After announcing the award, presenter [Jack Nicholson](/wiki/Jack_Nicholson "Jack Nicholson") was caught on camera mouthing the word "whoa" out of apparent surprise at the result.[[59]](#cite_note-59) The film's use of moral quandary as a storytelling medium was widely reported as ironic since many saw it as the "safe" alternative to *Brokeback Mountain*, which is about a [gay](/wiki/Gay "Gay") relationship (the other nominees, *[Good Night and Good Luck](/wiki/Good_Night_and_Good_Luck "Good Night and Good Luck")*, *[Capote](/wiki/Capote_(film) "Capote (film)")*, and *[Munich](/wiki/Munich_(2005_film) "Munich (2005 film)")* also tackle heavy subjects of [McCarthyism](/wiki/McCarthyism "McCarthyism"), homosexuality, and [terrorism](/wiki/Terrorism "Terrorism")).[[60]](#cite_note-60) Critic [Kenneth Turan](/wiki/Kenneth_Turan "Kenneth Turan") suggested that *Crash* benefited from [homophobia](/wiki/Homophobia "Homophobia") among Academy members,[[61]](#cite_note-61)[[62]](#cite_note-62) some of whom openly voiced their discomfort with *Brokeback Mountain* due to its subject matter.[[63]](#cite_note-63)[[64]](#cite_note-64)[[65]](#cite_note-65) After the Oscars telecast, critic [Roger Ebert](/wiki/Roger_Ebert "Roger Ebert") insisted in his column that the better film won the award.[[66]](#cite_note-66)[[67]](#cite_note-67)

*[Film Comment](/wiki/Film_Comment "Film Comment")* magazine placed *Crash* first on its list of "Worst Winners of Best Picture Oscars", followed by *[Slumdog Millionaire](/wiki/Slumdog_Millionaire "Slumdog Millionaire")* at #2 and *[Chicago](/wiki/Chicago_(2002_film) "Chicago (2002 film)")* at #3.[[68]](#cite_note-68) Similarly, a 2014 survey of film cri

Main articles: [Mission: Impossible 2 (score)](/wiki/Mission:_Impossible_2_(score) "Mission: Impossible 2 (score)") and [Mission: Impossible 2 (soundtrack)](/wiki/Mission:_Impossible_2_(soundtrack) "Mission: Impossible 2 (soundtrack)")

The film's [original score](/wiki/Film_score "Film score") was composed by [Hans Zimmer](/wiki/Hans_Zimmer "Hans Zimmer") and features vocals performed by [Lisa Gerrard](/wiki/Lisa_Gerrard "Lisa Gerrard").[[21]](#cite_note-23) In addition, the film includes contemporary music such as [Limp Bizkit](/wiki/Limp_Bizkit "Limp Bizkit")'s rendition of [Lalo Schifrin](/wiki/Lalo_Schifrin "Lalo Schifrin")'s [*Mission: Impossible* theme](/wiki/Theme_from_Mission:_Impossible "Theme from Mission: Impossible") entitled "[Take a Look Around](/wiki/Take_a_Look_Around_(song) "Take a Look Around (song)")" as well as [Metallica](/wiki/Metallica "Metallica")'s "[I Disappear](/wiki/I_Disappear "I Disappear")".[[22]](#cite_note-24)

While Ethan is rock climbing during his holiday, [Zap Mama](/wiki/Zap_Mama "Zap Mama")'s remixed version of "[Iko Iko](/wiki/Iko_Iko "Iko Iko")" plays on the soundtrack.

About the score, Zimmer said: "The love theme from *Mission: Impossible* [II] was written about six weeks before they started shooting. I was on it that early. Then, we had a big meeting in Australia. They had the love theme, and I knew what the story was about, and I always thought it was about these two men being in love with the girl. So I said to the record company guy, 'Look, here's one thing I would love you to do, when you find bands for me, make them all female. Make them all about sirens.' Of course, what did I get? A bunch of heavy metal bands with guys. I promise you, it would have been a better movie, and it would have been a better score."[[23]](#cite_note-25)

In 2024, Diego Pineda Pacheco from Collider singled out *Mission: Impossible 2* as one of Zimmer's most underrated scores especially for the *Injection* scene: "The film's score is imbued with Spanish influences, filling the romance at the core of the narrative with passion and flair."[[24]](#cite_note-26)

[Kangshung Face (the east face)](/wiki/Kangshung_Face "Kangshung Face") as seen from orbit

In 1856, Andrew Waugh announced Everest (then known as Peak XV) as 8,840 m (29,002 ft) high, after several years of calculations based on observations made by the [Great Trigonometrical Survey](/wiki/Great_Trigonometrical_Survey "Great Trigonometrical Survey").[[33]](#cite_note-39)
From 1952 to 1954, the [Survey of India](/wiki/Survey_of_India "Survey of India"), using [triangulation](/wiki/Triangulation "Triangulation") methods, determined that the height of Everest was 8,847.73 m (29,028 ft).[[34]](#cite_note-40) In 1975 it was subsequently reaffirmed by a Chinese measurement of 8,848.13 m (29,029.30 ft).[[35]](#cite_note-ABC_au-41) In both cases the snow cap, not the rock head, was measured.
The 8,848 m (29,029 ft) height given was officially recognised by Nepal and China.[[36]](#cite_note-42) Nepal planned a new survey in 2019 to determine if the [April 2015 Nepal earthquake](/wiki/April_2015_Nepal_earthquake "April 2015 Nepal earthquake") affected the height of the mountain.[[37]](#cite_note-43)

In May 1999, an American Everest expedition directed by [Bradford Washburn](/wiki/Bradford_Washburn "Bradford Washburn") anchored a [GPS](/wiki/Global_Positioning_System "Global Positioning System") unit into the highest bedroc
